General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

A Handful of Pistachios May Help You Sleep Better, Review Indicates

📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1079 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Could a handful of pistachios before you go to bed really help you sleep better?
  • A review of studies published in Nutrition Research Reviews examines how the nutrients and plant compounds in pistachios might influence sleep health.
  • Pistachios contain several nutrients linked to sleep-related processes, prompting an investigation into whether they might offer benefits beyond their nutritional value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Could a handful of pistachios before you go to bed really help you sleep better?

A review of studies published in Nutrition Research Reviews examines how the nutrients and plant compounds in pistachios might influence sleep health.

Pistachios contain several nutrients linked to sleep-related processes, prompting an investigation into whether they might offer benefits beyond their nutritional value.

While the findings suggest that pistachios may support sleep, the evidence is inconclusive and warrants further study.

“Pistachios are compelling for sleep research because they bring together several nutrients and plant compounds connected to sleep physiology within one whole food,” mentioned study author Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research in the Department of Medicine at Columbia University Institute of Nutrition, in a news release.

“Rather than focusing on a single ‘sleep nutrient,’ this review provides a rationale for studying how the complete pistachio food matrix may affect sleep-related pathways,” she continued.

The narrative review examined existing research on pistachios and sleep-related biology.

The researchers explored whether the combination of nutrients in pistachios could promote quality sleep.

Rather than identifying pistachios as a sleep remedy, the researchers outlined biological pathways through which their nutrients and bioactive compounds might influence sleep.

“We were particularly interested in pistachios because they are particularly high in phytomelatonin, polyphenols, and carotenoids, which we noted were plant-derived components that had been shown to have sleep benefits in preclinical studies,” St-Onge told Healthline.

“We also noted their high content of tryptophan and vitamin B6, which are relevant to melatonin production in humans,” she continued.

Pistachios contain several nutrients associated with sleep, including melatonin, which helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle.

Other studies examining the effects of some of these nutrients on sleep offer further context.

According to recent reports, A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of tryptophan supplementation found that it may reduce wakefulness after sleep onset, particularly at doses of at least 1 gram (g) daily. However, an ounce of pistachios supplies only about 71 mg, which is much less than the doses examined by the researchers.

Additionally, a 2023 review of dietary polyphenols led by St-Onge identified potential links between plant compounds and sleep outcomes, although results varied across studies.

Neither review established that polyphenols or tryptophan from pistachios specifically affected sleep quality.

“I was not surprised that pistachios may help support sleep, given their combination of nutrients involved in sleep regulation,” said Michelle Routhenstein, MS, a preventive cardiology dietitian at EntirelyNourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“Pistachios provide tryptophan, an amino acid the body uses to produce serotonin and melatonin; vitamin B6, which supports these pathways; and magnesium, which plays a role in nervous system function and sleep regulation,” she told Healthline.

The latest review highlights the concept of the “food matrix,” or how nutrients and bioactive compounds interact within a whole food.

Instead of investigating tryptophan, magnesium, or melatonin individually, researchers were curious about the combined effects of consuming them together in pistachios.

In a recent development, laboratory and simulated-digestion research offers clues about how fiber and plant compounds in pistachios and peanuts interact with gut microbes. However, these findings do not establish that eating pistachios changes sleep quality in real-world conditions.

Broader nutrition research also points to a relationship between diet and sleep.

It has been revealed that A 2021 review in the Annual Review of Nutrition examined evidence linking dietary patterns and individual nutrients to sleep outcomes. The findings suggest a relationship between sleep and diet, but note that more research is needed to determine cause and effect.

In a nutshell, the current evidence builds a compelling case for pistachios as a sleep aid.

However, it’s too soon to recommend pistachios as a sleep remedy, as many factors may affect sleep quality and insomnia.

Sources indicate that “Sleep difficulties can have different underlying causes,” Routhenstein noted. “If inadequate intake of these nutrients is a contributing factor, pistachios may help, but they may not address sleep concerns related to other nutrient deficiencies or other causes.”.

Much of the supporting evidence cited in the review comes from studies of individual nutrients, other foods, laboratory experiments, or biological mechanisms rather than from trials involving whole pistachios.

Researchers have also reported significant variations in the melatonin content of pistachios, making the amount in a typical serving difficult to pinpoint.

Additionally, the review received support from American Pistachio Growers, and the corresponding author, St-Onge, serves on its advisory board. Larger studies and clinical trials are needed, ideally without industry funding, to ensure well-rounded results.

Indeed, the authors call for randomized controlled trials examining whether eating pistachios affects sleep outcomes, including sleep quality, duration, and melatonin levels.

“This was a review; we noted that the complete profile of pistachios would make them well-suited to support healthful sleep, but research is needed to evaluate this,” St-Onge told Healthline.

“This is the next step, and something we are actively working on. We also need to better understand what dosage and frequency of consumption would be optimal.”.

Regardless, a handful of pistachios is still considered a healthy choice as part of a balanced diet.

Industry observers note that “A small handful, about 1 ounce of shelled pistachios, is an appropriate portion,” Routhenstein noted. “Enjoy them during the day or as a light afternoon or evening snack when you’re hungry.”.

If nutrients like tryptophan help promote sleep, it’s possible that other nuts could yield similar results.

“Other nuts, such as almonds and walnuts, may offer similar benefits because they also contain nutrients involved in sleep regulation,” Routhenstein noted.

“Early research is encouraging, but it’s too soon to say how much they might help.”.

Other foods, like turkey, also contain tryptophan.

Sources indicate that “For someone allergic to nuts, foods such as tofu, beans, oats, eggs, dairy, and fish can provide tryptophan, which the body uses to make serotonin and melatonin,” Routhenstein stated. “The goal is to meet their nutrient needs rather than rely on one food to improve sleep.”.

Sleep health depends on multiple factors. As such, Routhenstein recommends a personalized approach to getting better sleep, from what you eat and when you eat to addressing any nutritional gaps.

“I would also encourage regular, balanced meals throughout the day to support blood sugar management, especially for those with diabetes, while avoiding large meals close to bedtime,” Routhenstein said. “Caffeine later in the day and alcohol in the evening are also worth considering as possible sleep disruptors.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that on the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England.
  • The sex and weight have not been announced yet, and the calf also does not have a name.
  • It has been revealed that at birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England. Even more exciting, CCTV cameras captured the poignant moment for this threatened species. The footage shows rhino mom Asha giving birth, and the calf’s first unsure steps into the world.

The sex and weight have not been announced yet, and the calf also does not have a name.

It has been revealed that at birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds. By comparison, the largest adult greater one-horned rhinos weigh over two tons, or as much as a car.

In a recent development, the team used a combination of experience and non-invasive testing to help strategy out the pregnancy. They closely monitored Asha’s behavior and regularly collected samples of her poop. By testing hormone levels in the samples, they could track Asha’s reproductive cycle and identify when she would be most open to mating. This helped the team safely introduce her to Beni the rhino, while a separate analysis helped confirm the pregnancy.

Recent findings suggest that “Asha was pregnant for about 15 months, so it’s a long wait! We had our fingers crossed when she highlighted signs of labour and we knew we were likely to welcome the calf very soon,” Emma Evison, Team Manager for rhinos said in an e-mailed statement. “It was a big moment for us—and for the conservation breeding programme—when the calf arrived. Any birth can be risky, even for an experienced mum, but fortunately everything went smoothly. The calf was up and about within an hour and feeding shortly afterwards. Asha knows exactly what she’s doing.”.

Both mother and calf are reportedly in good health. They remained inside for the first few days following the birth to stay warm, but are now venturing to a special behind-the-scenes paddock outside of the enclosure. The calf is Asha’s fourth with father Beni. Sadly, Beni died in September following a sudden and brief illness.

“Beni was a lovely rhino. He was calm and approachable, helped train animal care specialists and even took part in animal behaviour studies,” added Tom Garland, Assistant Manager of the rhino team at Chester Zoo. “It’s lovely to know that his legacy lives on through this calf.”.

While not the largest rhino species in the world, greater one-horned rhinos stand about six feet tall at the shoulder and are the biggest in Asia. They have the smallest horns of any rhino, but also have the biggest teeth. The males will sometimes use these chompers to bite each other while sparring. At the moment, about 4,000 greater one-horned rhinos are alive today. They live in India and Nepal, in forests, wetlands, and grasslands. In the early 1990s, trophy hunting and habitat loss almost drove them to extinction.. Poaching for their prized horns also threatened their survival.

Industry observers note that while the IUCN Red List of Endangered Species currently lists them as Vulnerable, they remain  at risk of extinction. Many of the rhinos are concentrated into a relatively small number of protected areas, putting their genetic diversity at risk. A lack of genetic diversity can lead to inbreeding and worse health outcomes in general. This new calf is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding program to help maintain a healthy and genetically diverse population of greater one-horned rhinos living in human care.

In a recent development, “Supporting Asha’s pregnancy has been really exciting,” added conservation scientist John O’Hanlan. “She’s one of relatively few greater one-horned rhinos in Europe actively breeding, so every successful birth is important in maintaining a healthy and genetically diverse population.”.

Industry observers note that we always research products thoroughly before including them, and test every single one. Our reviews are thorough, in-depth, and honest. We put ourselves in the shoes of the shopper (because most of the time, we are the ones shopping!), and make sure that we’re answering the questions that we would want answered in the buying process.

It has been revealed that we favored natural-looking trees that are easy to set up. We also took shipping into account and tested trees that arrive not only in style, but with speed.

All trees that were reviewed were unboxed, set up (and lit up) by our contributors. They lived with trees and experienced all they had to offer firsthand, so that they could share the real deal with our readers.

What Size Christmas Tree Is Right for Me?

First and foremost, the height of your fake Christmas tree should depend on the height of your ceiling. A good rule of thumb is to keep your tree at least one-and-a-half feet lower than your ceiling, otherwise, it will look crowded. “I like to leave about six to12 inches between the top of the tree and the ceiling, so it feels intentional, not squeezed in,” indicates Shea McGee (more on the designer’s holiday advice below). Both McGee and Jeff Leatham, the floral designer who helped mastermind Kendall Jenner’s festive holiday house, agree that seven to eight feet hits a sweet spot in most homes. “The goal is balance: A tree that feels full and joyful but still lets the room breathe,” says McGee.

Who Should Buy Fake Christmas Trees?

Some people want to avoid the hassle (and extra cost) of buying a fresh tree each year, while others are allergic to real trees or are concerned about the fire safety hazard that comes along with real trees (they can become highly flammable as they dry out). Others (including people with pets) know that a real Christmas tree can be bait for disaster. Fresh or faux is really a matter of personal preference, and anyone who wants a fake Christmas tree should go for it. Leatham points out that in faux trees, the branches don’t drop, the coloring stays vibrant, and there’s often more structure to add extra ornaments.

Is It Better to Get a Pre-Lit Tree Or to Do It Yourself?

Choosing if you want your tree pre-lit is one of the first decisions you’ll make when navigating the vast artificial tree world. Pre-lit options are the preference of holiday decor gurus like Leatham. “Always, always, always go for prelit—it makes the tree look more full and realistic,” he tells us. Our editors like that pre-lit Christmas trees are convenient to set up (opposed to blindly garlanding string lights) and how they help guarantee your lighting scheme will look uniform. That said, drawbacks include potentially difficult repairs. While you can easily unstring removable lights to troubleshoot, built-in LEDs might pose bigger technical concerns. On the other hand, stringing your own lights may be a more complex, time-consuming process, but you’ll ultimately have more control over which areas of your tree are spotlighted.

How Should You Decorate Your Christmas Tree?

You’ve gotten your tree up, fluffed the branches, and poured yourself a nice cup of hot cocoa or eggnog to celebrate—now comes the fun part: decorating. While there’s no right way to decorate your Christmas tree, we looked through our archives for some tips and tricks to give your setup some extra sparkle.

It has been revealed that if your mentality is “more is more,” your holiday hero will be Kathy Hilton, who greeted AD back in 2021 with four artificial Christmas trees decked out with all the bells and whistles (emphasis on the bells). One tip we’d steal from Hilton is the idea that the decorations don’t have to go up all at once. “I normally start decorating in October, then keep adding until December,” claims Hilton.

Kendall Jenner, on the other hand, favors a more traditional tree, dipped in nostalgic classics like tinsel, twinkle lights, and vintage Christopher Radko ornaments that were passed down by her mother, Kris. Her designer reveals that she even loves stringing popcorn for the tree and dried orange slices on garlands. “Every year, more and more of my clients want more traditional holiday decorations that they can invest in, collect, and pass on to other generations,” claims Leatham. “I love that idea of seeing the same ornaments every year and having them bring back wonderful memories.” Since we have a feeling you have your own collection of heirloom Christmas decorations that have been collecting dust, we’d look to the supermodel for inspiration.

Color scheming your ornament display is one way to set yourself apart from the pack. “Red and green are traditional Christmas colors, but I love to break away from tradition and use bright jewel tones to create a dramatic and sophisticated look for the holiday season,” says Annie Sloan, color expert and creator of Chalk Paint. Stylist Dorcia Kelley of Kelle Miles Studio also suggests using a planter instead of a traditional tree stand or skirt for a modern look. “When hanging ornaments, you want to make sure you’re hanging it towards the end of the branch instead of right at the tip. This way, they’ll be more stable,” she says.

We also recommend playing with shapes, textures, and finishes to create as much interest as possible. AD’s perfect Christmas tree (pictured at the top of this article) features lots of vintage-inspired John Derian ornaments that bring on the kitsch, accented with classic ball ornaments in a range of sizes to create depth and dimension. A color palette of muted blue and bold metallic hues complement the deep green branches while slivers of silver tinsel add holiday pizzazz.

Fluffing your artificial Christmas tree is the key to convincingly faking the real thing. Most of the time, your tree will arrive with all the branches up-turned straight out of the box, and you’ll first want to mount the tree in its stand or collar. Next comes the actual fluffing—as reviewer Pujah Shah mentioned, it’s a smart idea to wear some work gloves to avoid any pricking that might occur while you’re working through the branches. Starting at the bottom, you’ll fan the largest branches down, layer by layer, until you reach the very top (where the branches become much shorter). If your branches have smaller tips built in, we like the center-right-left method of starting toward the base of the tree and positioning the smaller tips first center, next towards the right, and lastly towards the left, until you’ve reached the end. After that, you’ll go branch by branch, noticing that your tree looks full and much more lush with each adjustment. Afterwards, all that’s left to do is make any minor fixes to eliminate bald spots and voila!

What’s the Best Real Christmas Tree to Buy?

Recent findings suggest that again, that’s completely a matter of personal preference. Trees come in a variety of hues, some with a dark green, some with a blue tint, and others with a bright shade. Some have spiky needles while others are soft to the touch. Trees vary by geographical region and what's native to your area, but some of the most popular options used as Christmas trees across the U.S. include the Fraser Fir, Balsam Fir, Douglas Fir, and Blue Spruce (all of which are available in faux varieties, as well!).

How Does the Lifetime Cost of a Faux Tree Compare to Annually Buying a Real Tree?

According to recent reports, while how much your real Christmas tree costs will vary depending on its size as well as where you live in the United States, expect to spend anywhere from $40 to well over $100. In a few years, that running total will start to cost you, but with an artificial tree, you’ll pay the total cost up front. High-quality trees can also last you up to 15 years, making the sometimes extravagant price tags more digestible, especially in the later years when you’re no longer burdened with figuring out the logistics of strapping that netted Douglas Fir onto the car roof.

What Is Flocking and How Do You Do It?

Flocking refers to the process of dusting your artificial Christmas tree with a powdery white overcoat to mimic the appearance of fresh snowfall. Some trees—like the Yaheetech tree Brie Schwartz tested—come pre-flocked, but if you prefer a DIY moment, ready-to-flock sprays are also available at most big box retailers. We like Balsam Hill’s guide to flocking your tree, which details a recipe for homemade flocking, as well as all the safety precautions you’ll want to take: Like wearing protective gear, flocking in a well-ventilated environment, and ensuring you’re using non-hazardous materials. (Though if your budget allows, we think it might be best to invest in one of the brand’s ready-flocked trees.).

Industry observers note that king of Christmas vs. Balsam Hill.

Sources indicate that in the grand scheme of artificial Christmas trees, King of Christmas and Balsam Hill are widely known as the crème de la crème, thanks to their realistic appearance, convenient setup, and thoughtful extras like complimentary storage bags for the off-season. While both fall into the category of more luxuriously-priced holiday decor, Balsam Hill’s price points are slightly higher ($349 to $4,000+ while King of Christmas ranges from $229 to $3,000+).

Recent findings suggest that in our own quests for the most elite faux trees, we’ve also tried both brands. Commerce vice president Divya Viswanathan called Balsam Hill’s Fraser Fir “the Christmas tree of my dreams,” while contributor Andrea Lewis previously called her Blue Spruce from the brand “a lovely addition to our holiday traditions—elegant, easy to manage, and captures that cozy, Christmas air perfectly.” AD’s global director of audience development Pujah Shah became a King of Christmas convert last holiday after testing the brand’s Alpine Fir tree. “I wanted something tall, sleek, and a little bit dramatic that felt intentional in a modern space but still cozy enough for family chaos—it nails both,” indicates Shah. We think that both brands are great options—it’s hard to beat how realistic Balsam Hills designs are, and holiday floral designer and one of our experts, Jeff Leatham even named King of Christmas as his favorite brand. To choose the right brand for you, we recommend figuring out what will suit your space and your decorations, as well as establishing a price point you’re comfortable with.

We tapped the designer and creative force behind one of our favorite interior brands, McGee & Co., on the best ways to make your artificial Christmas tree really pop this season. Read on for her advice on how to make merry with a beautiful, yet intentional holiday set up.

Is There Such a Thing as an Ideal Sized Christmas Tree?

“When you’re choosing a tree, the ideal size really depends on your space. I like to leave about 6–12 inches between the top of the tree and the ceiling, so it feels intentional, not squeezed in. For most standard spaces, a 7-7.5-foot tree hits the sweet spot. If you have tall ceilings, you can absolutely go bigger—9-12 feet fills the volume beautifully. And in smaller rooms, a slimmer silhouette keeps things festive without overwhelming the layout. The goal is balance: A tree that feels full and joyful but still lets the room breathe.”.

What are Some of the Design Benefits of Choosing an Artificial Christmas Tree Versus a Real One?

In a recent development, “I love the flexibility an artificial tree gives you. You know exactly what shape and fullness you’re getting, and the branches stay right where you want them—which makes decorating so much easier and more polished. They also hold up all season long, which is great if you like to decorate early. And of course, you can reuse them year after year, which means you can invest in the style you love and bring it back every holiday.”.

How Do You Make an Artificial Christmas Tree Look More Realistic?

According to recent reports, “Start with a tree that already has a natural, realistic base—good branch texture goes a long way. From there, keep your palette cohesive so the whole tree feels curated instead of busy. I love layering garlands because they add that organic movement you see in real trees. Then finish with meaningful ornaments, ribbon, and a few organic touches—like dried citrus or pinecones. Those add warmth and authenticity, making even a faux tree feel beautifully lifelike.”.

“Both options have their place. A pre-lit tree is all about ease—the lights are perfectly placed, and you get that warm glow the minute you plug it in. It’s great if you want a beautiful tree without the extra steps. An unlit tree gives you more creative freedom. You can layer different styles of lights, change the mood from year to year, and really customize the look. It takes a bit more time, but it can feel incredibly intentional. So, if you want quick and polished, go pre-lit. If you love the process of styling every detail, unlit is the way to go.”.

In a recent development, the easiest way to make your artificial Christmas tree look like a real tree is to, well, cover it up. Go heavier on the decorations this year: Think garland, Christmas lights, pinecones, ornaments, a tree topper, etc. We're talking the works. Check out our go-to holiday decor tips that will make the best Christmas trees look even more magical.

Sources indicate that it’s affordable in bulk, doubles as a garland, and covers quite a bit of real estate from low to high. And who doesn’t love a bow? We pulled an option to satisfy the minimalists as well as some embellished trim that’s got major maximalist appeal.

A dead giveaway—no pun intended—that your tree’s a fake is the base: that plastic, mechanical-esque tree stand. Cover that metal stand up with a festive tree skirt (or basket!) as you would with real Christmas trees.

According to recent reports, if your tree doesn’t have pre-strung lights, head to the holiday aisle for some white or multicolored lights. Some of our favorites include unconventional and more delicate-looking lights that don’t necessarily scream “Christmas.” They’ll draw the eye to the center of the tree and take the attention off of the branches. Besides, you can never have too many lights in your home decor during the holiday season.

When scouting out ornaments for your tree, look for options with serious heirloom potential. Kendall Jenner’s Christopher Radko’s classic ornament collection is a good example—and Etsy sellers have troves of vintage ornaments to start your own traditions or recreate the supermodel’s holiday style. These miniature bulbs we found at Terrain are a fun way to create more depth when paired with larger balls, and we like that the different colors really pop when your tree is lit. We also turned to John Derian for gorgeous, traditional options pictured on our tree.

ACOG Strongly Recommends Hormone Therapy for Menopause Symptoms

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (913 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) published updated recommendations for menopause management in Obstetrics & Gynecology on October 15.
  • Recent findings suggest that these expanded recommendations are the most comprehensive guidance to date.
  • According to the ACOG guidance, 50%–92% of females experiencing menopause report VMS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) published updated recommendations for menopause management in Obstetrics & Gynecology on October 15.

Recent findings suggest that these expanded recommendations are the most comprehensive guidance to date. They include new clinical guidelines for menopause hormone therapy (MHT), nonhormonal medications, and nonpharmacological treatment of vasomotor symptoms (VMS), which include hot flashes and night sweats, and sleep and mood changes.

According to the ACOG guidance, 50%–92% of females experiencing menopause report VMS.

Around 16%–66% of females in the United States report menopause-related sleep issues, and more than one-third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal females report experiencing depressive symptoms.

“In recent years, misconceptions about the risks of hormone therapy have been widespread, which has made some clinicians reluctant to prescribe it and some patients hesitant to use it,” Bruce Pier, MD, clinical professor and associate fellowship director at the University of North Carolina and collaborator on the ACOG clinical practice guidelines, told Healthline.

Industry observers note that “This guidance offers a comprehensive review of the evidence to support individualized counseling and shared decision making. Our hope is that it clears up those misconceptions and expands access to treatment.”.

The ACOG is also developing companion guidance for genitourinary syndrome of menopause, expected in 2027.

The ACOG strongly recommends the use of MHT with estrogen and progestogens (or estrogen alone for people without a uterus) for both VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbance, in individuals who can use hormones.

It also conditionally recommends conjugated estrogen plus bazedoxifene (Duavee) as an alternative for these issues.

According to a meta-analysis from 2021 that was cited by the guidelines, estrogen therapy, with or without progestogens, significantly reduced VMS frequency and severity compared to a placebo or no treatment. A 2017 meta-analysis ranked transdermal estradiol plus a progestogen as the most effective option for reducing VMS frequency.

According to recent reports, A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis, also cited by the guidelines, found that MHT was associated with improved self-reported sleep quality. Once again, transdermal therapies indicated some of the largest effects.

The ACOG recommends initiating MHT before age 60 or within 10 years of the onset of natural menopause..

Recent findings suggest that it also suggests that the decision to start MHT for VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbances should be based on a shared decision making discussion about an individual’s symptoms and the benefits and risks of therapy. Consideration should also be taken regarding an individual’s:.

Research shows that factors such as race, culture, socioeconomic status, gender identity, and sexual orientation can influence how individuals experience menopause and the care they receive.

According to the SWAN study, Black women reported more menopause symptoms than white women but were less likely to be treated for them.

Industry observers note that “This updated document shines a light on these inequities. Clinicians can proactively help right now by asking every patient in midlife about symptoms, rather than waiting for them to bring it up. Long term, we hope this document drives more research funding to understand these gaps and begin closing them,” said Pier.

The ACOG stated in the guidelines that, “The available evidence is insufficient to recommend for or against the use of estrogen–progestogen or estrogen-only MHT for the treatment of menopause-related depressive symptoms.”.

It recommends that perimenopausal and postmenopausal individuals who meet the diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder (MDD) or those whose most noticeable symptom is depression should be treated according to depression management guidelines.

Current treatment guidelines for depression include therapy, medication, or a combination of the two.

Psychological treatments for depression include psychotherapy, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), while antidepressants are among the most commonly prescribed medications.

The ACOG strongly recommends the use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) for the management of menopausal symptoms like VMS and depression in individuals who don’t want to use MHT or can’t use it.

Currently, paroxetine is the only antidepressant that is approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the management of VMS.

The ACOG also strongly recommends the use of neurokinin receptor antagonists to manage VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbances in people who don’t desire hormone therapy or can’t use it.

There are currently two neurokinin receptor antagonists approved by the FDA to manage menopause symptoms. Fezolinetant (Veozah) was approved in 2023 to help manage hot flashes. In 2025, the FDA approved elinzanetant (LYNKUET) for the management of moderate to severe VMS due to menopause.

Another nonhormonal treatment for VMS that the ACOG conditionally recommends is gabapentin.

There are various nonpharmacologic treatments that the ACOG conditionally recommends for the management of VMS, vasomotor-related sleep disturbances, and mood changes. These are treatments that don’t involve the use of medications.

The nonpharmacologic treatments conditionally recommended include:.

It is generally recommended that these interventions are used alongside hormonal or nonhormonal medications.

The ACOG noted that there is not enough evidence to support the efficacy or safety of phytoestrogens, such as soy isoflavones, or herbal supplements, which are not regulated by the FDA in the same way medications are for safety, purity, or efficacy.

In a recent development, “Menopause is finally getting the attention it deserves, and this document reveals what evidence-based care should look like in this space. It lays out a range of safe, effective options for managing menopause symptoms. My message to anyone struggling with these symptoms is simple: talk to your clinician. You don’t have to suffer through them,” said Pier.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a latest Taycan or Macan EV.
  • Known as the Porsche 550 J, the pint-sized electric sports car will make its public debut at the Icons of Porsche festival in Dubai on November 21-22, celebrating 75 years of Porsche motorsport.
  • According to recent reports, if Hedley Studios sounds familiar, that’s because we’ve covered the manufacturer before, back when it was known as The Little Car Company.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a latest Taycan or Macan EV. In fact, it’s not even a full-sized car. Instead, the German automaker has teamed up with British luxury miniature car builder Hedley Studios to create an 80%-scale electric replica of one of Porsche’s most iconic racing cars, the legendary 550 Spyder.

Known as the Porsche 550 J, the pint-sized electric sports car will make its public debut at the Icons of Porsche festival in Dubai on November 21-22, celebrating 75 years of Porsche motorsport.

According to recent reports, if Hedley Studios sounds familiar, that’s because we’ve covered the manufacturer before, back when it was known as The Little Car Company. Among its more entertaining projects was a life-sized recreation of the famous Japanese Tamiya Wild One RC dune buggy, turning a childhood remote-controlled favorite into an actual drivable electric vehicle. We’ve also covered the company’s ultra-luxurious miniature electric cars, including its stunning Bentley Blower recreation.

Now the firm has turned its attention to Porsche, and the result is perhaps its most impressive miniature EV yet.

There’s something I love about miniature electric cars, combining the fun of four-wheels with the right-sized (or pint-sized) magic of mini-mobility.

The Porsche 550 J is based on the original 550 Spyder, Porsche’s first purpose-built racing sports car, which debuted in 1953 and went on to become a motorsport legend.

Despite being scaled down to 80% of the original’s dimensions, the new electric version still seats two adults. It weighs just 350 kg (772 lb), thanks partly to its lightweight tubular steel spaceframe and hand-formed carbon fiber bodywork.

The standard version features an 8 kW (11 hp) electric motor operating on a 48V system, providing a top speed of 40 mph (65 km/h) and a range of up to 30 miles (50 km).

Recent findings suggest that for those who want a bit more performance from their miniature Porsche, an optional RS Pack doubles the power to 16 kW (21 hp), increases the top speed to 50 mph (80 km/h), and extends the range to 50 miles (80 km) thanks to additional batteries. The upgrade also includes drilled disc brakes and adjustable suspension.

The attention to detail goes well beyond the exterior. The car features Brembo brakes, Bilstein suspension, Continental tires, and even a wood-rimmed Nardi steering wheel, just like the original. The classic dashboard retains its three-dial layout, though the fuel gauge has been replaced with a battery meter and the original choke lever now serves as a drive mode selector.

Even the charging port is cleverly hidden beneath the chrome fuel filler cap.

The project was developed in close collaboration with Porsche over six years, with Hedley Studios gaining access to original engineering drawings, archival materials, and historic vehicles in Porsche’s museum.

Only 250 examples will be produced, with buyers able to choose historic racing liveries or custom paint finishes, including colors matching their full-sized Porsches.

Of course, this level of craftsmanship doesn’t come cheap. Prices start at £69,500 (approximately US $91,000), before taxes and options. Orders are already open through Porsche dealers and Hedley Studios, with deliveries expected to begin in spring 2027.

That’s a lot of money for a car that’s only 80% there, but then again, this isn’t really meant to be practical transportation. It’s a collector’s piece that just happens to be electric, drivable, and capable of hitting 50 mph. When there are only 250 of these being built, the £70k price is really just the entry ticket to a special, ultra-luxury club of electric mini-Porsches.

And if you ask me, that sounds like a pretty fun combination. I don’t think I’ll ever be in the market for one of these personally, but I’d sure love to be friends with someone who is!

#213138. Christina Applegate ‘Not Happy at All’ After Learning She Was Misdiagnosed With MS

Christina Applegate ‘Not Happy at All’ After Learning She Was Misdiagnosed With MS

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health enhancement on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.
  • The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.
  • Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health enhancement on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.

The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.

Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.

In two podcast episodes released October 20, Applegate revealed that doctors had told her she was misdiagnosed with MS.

In a recent development, “She came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’ ” Applegate said as she fought back tears. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”.

The “Anchorman” and “Dead to Me” actor explained that her symptoms have continued to worsen, leaving her without an explanation for what she’s experiencing as doctors investigate the cause.

Being misdiagnosed with MS is relatively common. Applegate’s revelation highlights a difficult reality for people living with unexplained symptoms resembling MS. Her experience raises questions about how MS is diagnosed, why misdiagnoses may occur, and what people can do when their symptoms don’t match their diagnosis.

Recent findings suggest that while MS can be difficult to diagnose, an accurate diagnosis can help people with the condition gain access to appropriate treatment. A misdiagnosis, on the other hand, may lead to unnecessary interventions and medication, and take an emotional toll over time.

“MS can be challenging to diagnose because there is no single test that confirms it in every case,” remarked Steve Allder, MD, consultant neurologist at Re:Cognition Health.

It has been revealed that “An incorrect diagnosis can have significant consequences. Someone incorrectly diagnosed with MS may experience considerable anxiety, undergo unnecessary investigations, or receive treatments with potential risks and side effects. Equally, if MS is missed, treatment may be delayed, potentially allowing further neurological damage,” Allder told Healthline.

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis underscores that MS misdiagnoses remain a concern.

Research suggests that around 15% of people diagnosed with MS may actually have another condition.

However, estimates vary across studies, with some reporting rates ranging from 5–41%.

While an accurate diagnosis can guide patients toward appropriate treatment, a mistaken one may lead to unnecessary medication, emotional distress, and years of uncertainty.

Newly introduced diagnostic guidelines offer hope for greater accuracy, but they also raise important questions about how doctors can adequately distinguish MS from other conditions.

“Research has shown that MS can be both overdiagnosed and underdiagnosed,” Allder remarked.

In a recent development, “Diagnosis relies on a combination of symptoms, neurological examination, MRI findings, and sometimes, additional tests. It is also important to recognize that diagnoses can evolve as upcoming evidence emerges. As neurologists, we must remain open to revisiting a diagnosis when symptoms or test results do not fit, ensuring patients receive appropriate treatment and support.”.

MS symptoms may vary widely and overlap with several other conditions. These may include:.

Because these conditions share certain features with MS, healthcare professionals should consider a patient’s full clinical profile rather than relying on a single symptom or scan.

“MS can cause numbness, tingling, muscle weakness, visual disturbances, balance problems, and fatigue. However, these symptoms are not unique to the condition,” Allder said.

“For example, numbness and tingling may indicate peripheral neuropathy, sometimes associated with diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency. Weakness or altered sensation may result from a trapped nerve or spinal cord compression. Migraines can cause visual disturbances and sensory symptoms, while inner-ear disorders may affect balance,” he continued.

Allder noted that fatigue is particularly nonspecific and may be associated with:.

He explained that, as a neurologist, he considers the pattern, duration, and progression of symptoms alongside examination findings.

According to recent reports, “No single symptom automatically indicates MS. A thorough assessment is essential to identify the underlying cause and ensure the patient receives appropriate treatment,” he said.

There is no single test that definitively confirms every case of MS.

Diagnosis typically involves reviewing symptoms, conducting neurological examinations, and evaluating MRI scans and laboratory results.

MRI findings may be tricky to interpret. Some white-matter spots resemble MS lesions but may result from migraine, aging, or other conditions. Misapplying diagnostic criteria or overlooking alternative explanations can also lead to mistakes.

“MRI abnormalities alone do not confirm MS,” Allder mentioned. “The diagnosis must be based on the overall clinical picture, with alternative explanations carefully considered.”.

Research also suggests that MS misdiagnosis rates may differ by sex.

Research shows females are 2.1 times more likely to be misdiagnosed with MS than males, highlighting the potential for diagnostic bias and differences in how symptoms are evaluated.

The updated MS diagnostic criteria published in 2025 offer a framework for improving diagnosis.

The updated guidelines introduce several important changes.

For instance, the optic nerve (the nerve connecting the eye to the brain) is now included as a fifth anatomical location for assessing evidence of MS.

The revised criteria also include new MRI biomarkers, such as the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions. These features can help doctors distinguish MS-related abnormalities from other conditions.

These changes may help doctors diagnose MS earlier and more accurately.

According to recent reports, if you experience persistent or recurring neurological symptoms, seek medical advice. Your doctor can assess your symptoms and, if applicable, refer you to a neurologist.

Sudden weakness, vision loss, or difficulty speaking requires urgent medical assessment, Allder noted.

“Depending on the findings, investigations may include MRI scans of the brain and spinal cord, blood tests, and, in some cases, a lumbar puncture,” Allder noted.

“It is key that results are interpreted alongside symptoms and examination findings, as no single test should determine the diagnosis in isolation.”.

Allder said that if you’re unsure about a diagnosis, you can ask your neurologist what evidence supports it and whether alternative health conditions have been considered.

Industry observers note that “A second opinion or follow-up assessment may be appropriate. The priority is an accurate diagnosis that leads to the right treatment and support,” Allder stated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we want to let you in on a secret: You can replicate the good night’s rest you get at luxury destinations by dressing your bed with the hotel-quality sheets.
  • In a recent development, to get down to the nitty-gritty of these sheets, a hotel bed dressed in a percale weave boasts a crisp look and feel, almost as if it were made from your favorite pressed button-down shirt.
  • In a recent development, many of our favorite places to buy bedding—including Italian luxury brands like Frette—even create custom bed linens like these for the best hotels around the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we want to let you in on a secret: You can replicate the good night’s rest you get at luxury destinations by dressing your bed with the hotel-quality sheets. Aside from accessories like fluffy down feather pillows and mattress toppers, we often attribute cotton percale and sateen to a five-star sleep.

In a recent development, to get down to the nitty-gritty of these sheets, a hotel bed dressed in a percale weave boasts a crisp look and feel, almost as if it were made from your favorite pressed button-down shirt. A sateen weave, however, is polished and resembles the appearance of pearls. What’s more, both of these high-quality sheets have breathable, wrinkle-resistant qualities for a refined aesthetic we know and love in a high-end establishment.

In a recent development, many of our favorite places to buy bedding—including Italian luxury brands like Frette—even create custom bed linens like these for the best hotels around the world. Scroll below for a staycation-style set of sheets.

For consistency, all of the prices reflect queen sizes. However, many brands offer twin size and king size options too.

It has been revealed that the Andersen Hotel, a family-owned boutique retreat in Copenhagen, offers guests sheets, towels, and robes from the editor-favorite brand Boll & Branch. To mimic the experience at home, you can shop the entire collection, including the Signature Hemmed Sheet Set tested and beloved by contributor Rachel Fletcher. The buttery-soft cotton sateen set is made with long-staple cotton fibers, and only gets softer with each wash. “That extra-soft feel, paired with the lovely, cooling properties, makes them feel like the luxury sheets they are,” Fletcher shares. After more than five years with these sheets, Fletcher adds that there are no signs of pilling or wear, “just that coveted softness which feels lived-in but not worn out.”.

Matouk is a legacy brand known for bespoke touches on high-thread-count sheets. Their hotel collection is found in a number of luxury resorts and historic inns, including Hotel Barrière Fouquet's in Latest York City and renowned Arizona wellness escape Castle Hot Springs. The Bergamo is their most lightweight percale sheet, combining Giza 87 and 92 Egyptian cotton yarns. “I hate scratchy sheets, and I breathed a sigh of relief when I slipped into these,” states contributor Allie Weiss. “They are lightweight, crisp-looking, and soft to the touch.” We also recommend taking advantage of their personalization feature, which allows you to add a monogram to the edge of the sheet. Just remember that each piece is sold separately, so you’ll have to build your own bedscape.

Another property with Frette bedding, The Palace Hotel in Madrid is an AD-favorite historic hotel. “You’ll definitely want to stop by La Cúpula during your trip for an afternoon drink and some bites from the stylish tapas menu,” notes shopping editor Audrey Lee. “If it’s the right time of day, the room becomes drenched in sunlight through the dome-shaped stained glass ceiling.” As for the bedding, you can mirror the hotel’s lavish interiors with Frette’s bold sheets. The polished sateen set boasts a thick border in six color combinations to wake up a bedroom.

Recent findings suggest that make a statement without sacrificing a classic hotel look with this tuxedo sheet set. Crafted by Frette for the Ritz-Carlton, this design includes a white-on-white stripe pattern that is perfect for a suite-inspired space. For a unique touch, you can also pair a set of the classic pillowcases with this set for a blend of solid colors and bold lines. Instead of shorter threads that can fray over time, this fabric is made of extra-long staple cotton sateen for an ultra-soft and durable feel.

According to recent reports, priding themselves on a sustainable outlook toward hospitality, the 1 Hotel Group offers a connection with nature and serenity even in the heart of the city. With green-certified buildings and a focus on wellness, it’s no surprise that this hotel’s bedding is equally natural. Kassatex’s 100% cotton sheets are softer than percale but not as shiny as sateen. Contributor Kate McGregor stayed at the 1 Hotel Seattle and was impressed with the breathability. “I’m quite a hot sleeper, but even after a cross-country flight, I slept soundly,” she states. “There was no swishing noise as I moved, either, a pet peeve of mine with really crisp hotel sheets.” Machine washable and available in either a queen or king set, these sheets come with a 60-day trial, so you can really get a feel for them without worrying about a wasted investment.

What Type of Sheets Do Five-Star Hotels Use?

While it varies from property to property, the majority of the hotels on this list use white cotton sheets. Whether percale or sateen, the best hotel sheets all offer a neat, design-agnostic look that suits the center of Newly introduced York just as well as the rolling hills of Tuscany. Percale will have an added crispness and cooling factor, while sateen will have an added shine and smoothness. Regardless of material finish, look for an all-natural fiber makeup (like 100% cotton) and a versatile white colorway.

Why Do Hotels Like to Use White Bed Sheets?

From an aesthetic perspective, white sheets offer a cloudlike, serene escape for the guest. They also look the cleanest. Stark white sheets cannot hide stains or wear and tear as darker colors can—you can see exactly where each thread has snagged. White bedding is also the most easily sanitized; it even has its own setting on your washing machine. Bleach is necessary to kill germs, especially in a commercial setting, and you don’t want to risk the color fading and yellow stains that can occur on colored sheets.

What Type of Sheets Does The Ritz-Carlton Use?

According to recent reports, the Ritz-Carlton uses white cotton sheets from luxury bedding brand Frette. The extra-long staple cotton is more durable than short strands, proven wash after wash. Boasting a subtle monochromatic stripe, The Ritz-Carlton’s sheets play with texture without departing from the clean lines and opulent energy of their suites' overall design scheme.

What Fabrics Are the Best Sheets Made of?

Long or extra-long-staple cotton sheets are considered the “best,” in our experience. These typically have a smooth finish and hold up well over time. That said, so much of it comes down to your own personal preferences. “[Deciding] which one is best for a particular person or climate is relative,” Katie Glusica, professor in the fibers department at the Savannah College of Art and Design, previously shared. “A percale in the 200 to 400 thread-count range will be durable and have a cooler sensation and a lighter weight feel, best for people who run a little warm or where the climate is warmer. Sateen sheets in the 300- to 600-thread-count range are best for someone looking for softness over durability, and better for cooler climates where a heavier feeling sheet is more comfortable.” Then, there are the more seasonal fabrics like airy linen for summer or thick flannel for winter. If you’re still undecided, we often find that Goldilocks-level comfort in cotton sheets with thread counts between 200 and 600 threads per inch.

What Are the Best Bed Sheets for Hot Sleepers and Cold Sleepers?

Recent findings suggest that while percale is recommended for hot or warm sleepers, compared to other cotton sheets, shopping writer Julia Harrison argues the best is bamboo or Tencel lyocell. “AD editors and I prefer these natural fibers because they usually feel cool and gentle against skin, but they also have great temperature regulating qualities since the fabric absorbs excess moisture to help you stay refreshed while you sleep,” she says.

And during the winter months, or for those who run cold year-round, there’s nothing more comforting than sinking into a bed dressed in flannel sheets. “These are great for keeping you cozy and toasty because of a brushed (and sometimes double-brushed) cotton material that feels soft to the touch,” claims senior shopping editor Nashia Baker. “It depends on the brand, but some make their sheets with 100% long-staple cotton, like supima cotton, that’s known for its durability without wear over time.”.

What Is the Difference Between Percale and Sateen?

It has been revealed that both are made from cotton, but the weave is what differentiates the two. “Percale is a classic one-over, one-under construction that creates a crisp, breathable fabric with a matte finish reminiscent of fine poplin shirting, while sateen’s longer thread float produces a smoother hand and subtle sheen,” Rebecca Weinstein, vice president of design at Highgate, the management company for the Atlas Hotel in Boston, previously told AD. Hot sleepers will feel most comfortable in cooling sheets like percale, while those who prefer a less structured, smooth feel will likely splurge on sateen. “Sateen is more dense, with more threads packed in, so the fabric is warmer,” shared Preeti Gopinath, associate professor of textiles and founding director of the MFA textiles program at Parsons School of Design in Latest York. “Percale is cooler, and with a thread count of 150 to 200, there is less fabric per square inch, which allows for better airflow.”.

  • In a recent development, it’s yet another vehicle nobody asked for, from a organization that ended Model S and Model X production this year and is about to end the Cybertruck.
  • Musk made the comments on stage at the Newly introduced York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk claims Tesla looks to build a version of the Model Y with no steering wheel and no pedals, a driverless people-mover he describes as “good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people.”.

In a recent development, it’s yet another vehicle nobody asked for, from a organization that ended Model S and Model X production this year and is about to end the Cybertruck. And the data notes very few car buyers want a car they can’t drive.

Musk made the comments on stage at the Newly introduced York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.

In a recent development, he pitched it as the answer to the Cybercab only carrying two people. “We still need autonomous vehicles if you’ve got 4 or 6, or a whole family,” Musk remarked, before adding that Tesla looks “an autonomous version of the Model Y that won’t have steering wheels or pedals.”.

There was no timeline, no price and no word on where it would be built.

Six or seven seats points straight at the Model Y L, the stretched three-row Model Y that Tesla launched in the US in July for $61,990, or the regular Model Y with the $2,500 seven-seat option Tesla brought back in January.

According to recent reports, here’s the funny part. When Tesla rolled out the Model Y L in China in August 2025, Musk said it might never come to the US, “given the advent of self-driving in America.”.

In a recent development, the idea was that autonomy would make a bigger family car pointless. Less than a year later, Tesla was building the Model Y L at Giga Texas and selling it at the top of the Model Y lineup.

According to recent reports, now Musk wants a driverless version of that same car. So families still need a big vehicle, self-driving or not. That’s what we stated in 2025.

Industry observers note that the robotaxi argument doesn’t hold up either. Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet is mostly Model Ys, and those cars have a steering wheel and pedals.

Industry observers note that the wheel isn’t what’s stopping them from driving themselves. Removing it mostly makes the car useless outside Tesla’s geofences.

We’ve already seen what that looks like. Tesla opened personal Cybercab orders last week at $29,990, but the car only works inside Robotaxi service areas and requires a $299 per month subscription to operate at all.

There’s also the regulatory mess. Tesla self-certified the Cybercab as compliant with federal safety standards even though FMVSS 135 calls for a foot-operated service brake, and NHTSA responded with a Special Order in September. Zoox took the slower route and got a Part 555 exemption, which caps it at 2,500 vehicles a year. A second vehicle with no controls means a second round of that fight.

According to recent reports, cox Automotive’s 2026 Autonomous Vehicle Study asked US consumers which level of autonomy they’d find most appealing in a vehicle they own. Only 10% picked fully driverless Level 5, down from 17% when Cox first asked in 2016.

The most popular choice was Level 4 at 28%: full autonomy, but with the option for a human to drive. And only 38% said they’d feel safe in a Level 5 vehicle, compared to 87% for a modern car with basic driver aids.

So after a decade of exposure to self-driving tech, interest in a car with no controls went down, not up.

Sources indicate that tesla already makes the Model Y. It already makes a six-seat Model Y. Just make the Model Y.

It has been revealed that in 2016, Musk’s Master Strategy Part Deux promised to “expand the electric vehicle product line to address all major segments.” Ten years later, once the Cybertruck ends next summer, Tesla’s consumer lineup is the Model 3 and Model Y. That’s it. No affordable car (Musk called a non-robotaxi $25,000 Tesla “pointless” in 2024), no compact crossover, no minivan, no midsize pickup.

Teslafsdtracker is the only real source of Tesla ADS/ADAS capability.

Sources indicate that it shows a safety critical intervention is needed every 2000 miles. That is less than 1% of whats needed to remove a human from the real time loop. Hence Tesla's hiding of intervention data and operational parameters, and the control centers where humans watch real time video feeds and initiate interventions when needed.

Industry observers note that tesla L4 is all smoke and mirrors. All they have is a L2 system driving in geo restricted zones with driver oversight shifted from the front seat to a control center.

In a recent development, every time there’s a gap in Tesla’s lineup, Musk gives the same answer: autonomy will fill it. The Model Y L was going to be unnecessary. The cheap car was pointless. The Model S and X made way for Optimus, and the Cybertruck for the Cybercab.

But Tesla’s own robotaxi fleet proves you don’t need to remove the steering wheel to run a robotaxi. Keeping it costs Tesla almost nothing and keeps the car useful for the roughly 90% of buyers who still want the option to drive. Taking it out only adds a federal compliance fight and shrinks the market to people who live inside a geofence.

If Tesla wants to sell more cars, it should build cars people are asking for. Who exactly is asking for this one?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first.
  • Recent findings suggest that first, a dash of history.
  • It has been revealed that the GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first. But the latest in that tradition, the 2027.5 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition, doesn’t just split the difference between 2027 and 2028; it also slides between the S and SE models that make up the lower tiers of the lineup, while bringing along some of the sweet features from the top-shelf GTI Autobahn trim. In other words, it has the makings of a Goldilocks special.

Recent findings suggest that first, a dash of history. “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S. and Canadian markets back in the days of the Mk1, including on the first GTI that arrived in 1979 in the Great White North and in ‘83 in the States. (The firm then returned to the Rabbit name for the Mk5 Golf here, but that’s less consequential—or memorable.) In honor of that first GTI, this upcoming trim includes an adorable little chrome bunny on its hatch, in addition to blacked-out mirror caps, grille, and other trim bits scattered around the exterior that replace red items on other members of the current GTI family.

It has been revealed that the GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record. The 19-inch black wheels come from the Golf R, and are wrapped as standard in summer performance tires, versus the all-season rubber that normally comes with less-expensive GTIs. But the most notable change on the fun side is the presence of the DCC adaptive dampers, for which you otherwise would have to spring for the top-shelf Autobahn trim to get. Inside, meanwhile, the Rabbit Edition picks up the GTI SE’s GTI Clubsport ArtVelours material on its comfy yet supportive front buckets and rear bench.

Like all other current GTIs, unfortunately, the Rabbit Edition forces buyers to use a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic to change the gears tied to its 241-horsepower turbocharged inline-four; the manual gearbox remains locked in the past. Still, if you can look past that, the Rabbit Edition has the makings of a steal. Volkswagen hasn’t unveiled pricing yet—that’ll come closer to its on-sale date of Q2 2027—but seeing as how the carmaker is quite explicit about where it lands in the lineup, expect it to come in the $36,250 of the GTI S and the $40,240 of the GTI SE, plus or minus any little price bumps they might pick up in the next half model year.

Industry observers note that will Sabel Courtney is a contributing editor at Road & Track. A 12-year veteran of journalism, he formerly worked at Gear Patrol, The Drive, and RIDES Magazine, and contributed to the New York Daily News and Jalopnik, among other outlets. You can often find him test-driving new cars in New York City, cursing the slow-moving traffic surrounding him.

Industry News: RFK Jr.’s Revised Vaccine Schedule May Cause 83% Surge in Hepatitis B Infections

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, health and Human Services Secretary Robert F.
  • Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.
  • A latest study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s proposed changes to the childhood vaccine schedule have raised alarm among public health experts and researchers.

Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.

A latest study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) ended its recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for the virus. Instead, the federal health agency recommends individual-based clinical decision making.

After reviewing the evidence, the CDC, which is overseen by the HHS, concluded that newborns “face little risk of contracting hepatitis,” which deemed the vaccine, typically administered at birth, unnecessary.

Experts say this shift in public health policy wasn’t based on science, and researchers warn of rising infection rates.

“Hepatitis B immunizations have been proven to protect individuals against a serious and significant disease,” said Graham Tse, MD, pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

Sources indicate that “The hepatitis B vaccines have several decades of history and have been proven safe and effective,” Tse remarked. “There has been no new data or evidence presented or uncovered to support delaying the newborn dose of hepatitis B.”.

Here’s what parents should know about making informed decisions with their child’s healthcare team.

Recent findings suggest that A U.S. modeling study published in Annals of Internal Medicine on October 20 projected that delaying the first vaccine dose until 2 months could increase chronic hepatitis B infections among infants by 19% under one scenario.

With shared decision making and lower vaccine uptake, projected increases ranged from 83% to 225%, compared with universal birth-dose vaccination.

The researchers also estimated that up to 1.8 million young adults could remain susceptible to hepatitis B by age 20 under shared decision making, compared with 232,000 under universal birth dosing.

Another study published in JAMA Pediatrics in late April projected hundreds of additional chronic infections annually if the hepatitis B birth dose were delayed or omitted.

However, these figures are model-based projections, rather than verified outcomes. Actual results will depend on vaccination rates and other factors.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) adopted a recommendation shifting away from universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).

Under the newly introduced approach, parents and healthcare professionals can decide together whether to give the first dose at birth or defer it until the baby is 2 months old.

It has been revealed that the change followed an 8 to 3 vote by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), marking a departure from longstanding U.S. guidance.

However, infants born to mothers who test positive for hepatitis B or whose infection status is unknown should still receive the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth, according to the updated guidelines.

Hepatitis B is a viral infection that affects the liver.

Although some infections resolve, newborns and infants face a higher risk of developing lifelong hepatitis B infection compared with adults.

Up to 90% of infants infected during their first year develop chronic hepatitis B.

“We have actual world evidence that vaccinating newborns for hepatitis B prevents hepatitis B infections later in life and the serious complications of that disease,” Tse mentioned.

Over time, chronic infection can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, or liver cancer.

“The danger of delaying the newborn hepatitis B shot is that individuals do not get vaccinated and thereby do not have protection against hepatitis B,” Tse stated.

Early vaccination helps protect young infants before potential exposure occurs, including situations in which maternal screening misses an infection.

“Newborns can be infected with hepatitis B from a mother who is not aware they have a hepatitis B infection or from exposure later in life,” Tse noted.

“The risk is developing a hepatitis B infection, which can potentially lead to liver cancer, fulminant hepatitis, or severe end-stage liver disease.”.

In contrast to the CDC, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) still recommends a universal hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth, followed by additional doses during infancy.

The leading pediatric medical organization has raised concerns about the potential consequences of reduced vaccination rates.

The hepatitis B vaccine has decades of safety and effectiveness data.

Tse stated the AAP’s vaccine schedule and recommendations are based on decades of study, use, and expert input, and provide the best protection against vaccine-preventable diseases.

Parents who have questions about potential side effects, timing, or their baby’s individual risk should discuss them with a qualified healthcare professional.

“Parents are confused, given the recommendations from CDC, HHS, and Kennedy differ from established and respected groups such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Infectious Disease Society of America, and several states,” Tse remarked.

“Parents desire to keep their children safe, and having differing opinions and confusion will lead to reduced vaccination rates as parents experience doubt as to whom to listen to or believe.”.

While the updated CDC policy offers more flexibility for some families, lower vaccination uptake could lead to an increase in chronic hepatitis B infections.

Ask your pediatrician about the benefits of vaccination against hepatitis B at birth, the risks of delaying the first dose, and the recommended schedule for completing the series.

You can also ask how maternal screening results affect your baby’s protection.

An informed conversation with your healthcare professional can help you weigh the evidence and choose a vaccination proposal for your baby.

“I see no argument whatsoever for changing the established vaccination schedule for hepatitis B,” Tse said.

“There have been no latest studies, no data, nor evidence to justify Kennedy’s proposed changes to the childhood immunization schedule. Delaying vaccinations or skipping vaccinations puts your child at risk for serious and significant diseases, which are all preventable,” Tse stated.

Latest Update: Aptera (SEV) completes its first customer solar EV — for its top crowdfunder

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, aptera (SEV) has finished building its first solar electric vehicle for a paying customer.
  • It has been revealed that it’s a real milestone for a company that has pushed back its delivery dates since 2022.
  • It has been revealed that aptera confirmed today from its Carlsbad, California headquarters that it completed what it calls its first production solar electric vehicle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, aptera (SEV) has finished building its first solar electric vehicle for a paying customer. It’s going to Martin Hartono, the startup’s No. 1 “Accelerator” investor, and it’s being exported out of the US.

It has been revealed that it’s a real milestone for a company that has pushed back its delivery dates since 2022. And it comes a week after Aptera reported $9.2 million in cash against the roughly $25 million it says it needs to start series production.

It has been revealed that aptera confirmed today from its Carlsbad, California headquarters that it completed what it calls its first production solar electric vehicle. The car is finished in “Noir,” a matte black exterior, and was built for Accelerator #1.

Industry observers note that accelerators are investors from Aptera’s community funding program, where delivery priority goes to whoever invests the most. So the first customer car went to the biggest check.

It has been revealed that hartono is the CEO of GDP Venture, the Jakarta-based venture arm of Indonesia’s Djarum Group. Aptera didn’t say which country the car is going to, what he paid for it, or when it will actually be handed over.

In the release, Hartono remarked Aptera is a fit for people who want to “minimize their energy consumption without compromising the ability to travel long distances.” Co-CEO Chris Anthony called it “the moment our team has worked toward for years” and said the tech giant is working to finish more vehicles for early customers as soon as possible.

No number was given for how many more.

The timing is interesting. Just seven weeks ago, Aptera cut its estimated cost to start production to about $25 million, down from $40 to $45 million, and noted the first 40 production vehicles would start building by the end of 2026, with customer deliveries in early 2027 “subject to financing.”.

Recent findings suggest that its Q3 report last week didn’t change that picture much. Aptera ended September with $9.2 million in cash, and $4.1 million of that is refundable reservation fees. It lost $14 million in the quarter, and its own filing indicates substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern “has not been alleviated.”.

On November 10, it priced a $6 million registered direct offering at $1.75 per share. SEV closed at $1.67 on Tuesday, with a 52-week high of $7.

Sources indicate that the solar side of the pitch holds up better. In August, TÜV Rheinland measured 4.23 to 4.75 kWh per day going into the battery from the car’s integrated panels in Carlsbad, which works out to roughly 40 miles of daily driving. But that conversion relies on Aptera’s 100 Wh/mile efficiency target, and today’s release itself notes that figure isn’t yet confirmed for production vehicles.

Industry observers note that the release’s risk factors are also worth reading. They list export, import, certification and registration requirements, state dealer licensing, single-source suppliers, and whether reservations will convert into binding orders. Shipping car No. 1 to an investor overseas sidesteps most of those for now.

Credit where it’s due. Aptera has a finished car built to a customer’s spec, which is more than Lightyear or Sono Motors ever got to before they ran out of money. We’ve followed this company since it came back in 2019, and plenty of people (us included, at times) didn’t think we’d see this day.

A positive achievement, but the question remains: Is this essentially a hand-built prototype and a token delivery to one very rich customer, or is it the first of many more vehicles that will roll off an assembly line for regular people over the next couple months?

Recent findings suggest that but I have to be honest, this looks more symbolic than like the start of a production ramp. This is a single vehicle, built before Aptera has raised the money it indicates it needs for series production, and it went to the person who put the most money into the company. That’s a thank-you and a good press release ahead of what will likely be another raise. It doesn’t tell us much about Aptera’s ability to build cars at a cost that works.

Recent findings suggest that the real test is still the first 40 cars, and whether they reach regular reservation holders in the US. Aptera says it needs about $25 million to get there. It has $9.2 million, $4.1 million of which customers can ask back for, and it’s raising money at under $2 a share, which means a lot of dilution for every dollar.

Industry observers note that we want this to work. Ultra-efficient cars are the only way vehicle-integrated solar makes sense, and Aptera is the last serious attempt standing. So can it fund those 40 cars before the cash runs out?

If you’re buying an EV, powering it with home solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero, even if your car doesn’t have panels built into the body like the Aptera.
